collection_summary: This instance is a curated, source-defined ground truth listing the 27 modern stock market crashes and bear markets from 1929 (Wall Street Crash) through 2025 whose Wikipedia master-list Notes column documents a clear proximate cause, as drawn from the chronological wikitable of the Wikipedia 'List of stock market crashes and bear markets' master article. For each crisis the staged row records the Year, Affected Region or Country, Cause Category (from a closed 6-value taxonomy curator-derived from the source's Notes column), and Specific Trigger (a brief curator-summarized phrase from the source's Notes column). The 27-row universe is the 'Year ≥ 1929 AND Notes column documents a clear proximate cause' subset of the master article's 60-row chronological list: first the temporal filter narrows the list to those starting in 1929 or later, anchored at the iconic Wall Street Crash and excluding pre-1929 events that cluster heavily in 19th-century US/UK banking panics; then the cause-documentation filter drops 10 of the year-filtered candidates whose Notes column is empty or describes only magnitude/timeline without identifying a cause. The schema is designed for benchmark evaluation: Crisis is the PK lookup target; Year is exact-match numeric; Affected Region is exact-match from a fixed vocabulary; Cause Category is exact-match from a closed 6-value taxonomy; Specific Trigger is semantic-match free-text.
source_coverage_notes:
Roles:
- source_urls[0] (List_of_stock_market_crashes_and_bear_markets): universe + filter + value (defines the canonical 60-row chronological-crashes wikitable; the 27 staged rows are filtered via 'Year ≥ 1929 AND Notes column documents a clear proximate cause'; supplies the per-row Crisis name verbatim from the Name column, Year from the Date column, Affected Region from the Country column with NaN-resolution from Notes column context, and base material for Cause Category and Specific Trigger derivation from the Notes column).

Single-source Tier B instance. The Wikipedia master article is the canonical chronological compilation of financial crises and stock market crashes. Per-row cells: Crisis name, Year, and Affected Region are verbatim/lightly-normalized from the source's Name/Date/Country columns; Cause Category is curator-derived from the source's Notes column applying a 6-value closed taxonomy; Specific Trigger is a 1-line curator paraphrase of the source's Notes column. Cell-level audit can spot-check by reading the master article's wikitable for any of the 27 staged events; the Cause Category assignment is the curator-judgment cell most likely to attract audit attention, but the 6-value taxonomy is clearly defined and assignments are documented per-row in normalization_decisions.
decision_log:
Candidate card (per instance_selection_priorities.md):
- Pre-gate verdict: Pass. Universe (27 stock market crashes and bear markets 1929-2025 whose Notes column documents a clear proximate cause; post-cycle-3) is fully source-defined via the cited master article's chronological wikitable and the dual-clause filter 'Year ≥ 1929 AND Notes column documents a clear proximate cause'; partition rule (per crisis) is source-defined; per-row attribute cells are source-grounded via the master article's Name/Date/Country/Notes columns (Year, Affected Region directly; Cause Category and Specific Trigger derived from the Notes column with curator judgment). Table is LLM-knowable for a pre-2025 cutoff: very-LLM-knowable cells include canonical crises (1929 Wall Street, 1987 Black Monday, 2000 Dot-com, 2008 financial crisis, 2020 COVID); mid-difficulty cells include well-known but less-iconic events (1992 Black Wednesday, 1997 Asian, 1998 Russian, 2010 Euro); harder calibration cells include obscure events (1971 Brazilian, 1989 Rio de Janeiro, 1989 Friday the 13th, 2009 Dubai standstill, 2024 China property, 2024 Tokyo yen-carry, 2025 tariffs). Row count (27) is well above the 10-row gate.
- Seed/provenance: original instance, NOT from a seed in example_questions.txt. User selected from a causal #4 candidate slate (aviation crashes, financial crises, maritime disasters, bridge collapses, presidential assassinations, hyperinflation events), choosing financial crises with deep-dive on schema design from a benchmark-evaluation angle.
- Category: causal (gap 2; this instance brings causal from 3/5 to 4/5 — gap 1 near-saturation) primary; temporal (gap 3) secondary because the Year column spans 1929-2025 providing a meaningful temporal axis. Per references/artifact-contract.md, causal pairs canonically with operation_type=projection (when the schema includes a Cause cell as one of the projected attributes); the db_analog 'SELECT ... FROM modern_financial_crises WHERE year BETWEEN 1929 AND 2025 AND notes_column_documents_clear_proximate_cause = TRUE' is the canonical causal-projection-over-dual-clause-filtered-universe primitive.
- Source plan: Tier B Wikipedia, single source URL; gt_construction = manual_wikipedia; source_count = 1.
- Expected shape: 27 rows × 5 columns; PK = Crisis (post-cycle-3 state; total drops from the year-filtered cycle-0 candidate set: 10 rows whose Notes column has no clear proximate cause).
- Domain: Business/Economics — third Business instance (existing: g20_countries_attributes, eurozone_adoptions_1999_2023). Financial crises is a natural Business/Economics angle that complements the existing Business instances (G20 country attributes are about national economies; eurozone adoptions are about monetary union; financial crises are about cyclical economic disruptions).
- Risks/adaptation: (a) Cause Category is curator-derived from the source's Notes column. The 6-value taxonomy (Speculative bubble / Real estate bubble / Sovereign debt crisis / Currency crisis / External shock / Margin/leverage failure) is well-defined but assignments require judgment for events with multiple contributing causes — e.g., 1990 Early 1990s recession had both Iraqi oil shock and Fed monetary aspects but is staged as 'External shock' per the source's primary framing. (b) Some events (1937, 1990, 2008) have causes spanning multiple categories; the staged Cause Category is the dominant cause per the Wikipedia Notes column's primary framing. (c) Region cells for 2 rows currently in the universe where source has NaN Country (1997 Oct mini-crash, 2001 9/11 attacks) are resolved from the Notes column context — these are curator-derived but defensible. (d) Specific Trigger cells are curator-paraphrased 1-line summaries of the source's Notes column; they are semantic-match-evaluable rather than exact-match.
- Decision: Stage.

Why original rather than seed-driven: no seed in example_questions.txt targets financial crises or causal-style historical events.

Why schema B (5 cols) rather than alternatives: deep-dive schema design considered 3 options. Schema A (4 cols, all exact-match-evaluable: Crisis + Year + Region + Cause Category) was the most automation-friendly but lost specificity ('Banking panic' doesn't distinguish 1907 from 1929). Schema C (6 cols, adding a Severity Metric) was rejected because severity metrics vary across sources (Dow vs S&P vs local index; cross-event comparability is hard). Schema B (5 cols, the chosen design) balances evaluability with specificity: 3 of 5 cells are exact-match (Year, Region, Cause Category), Specific Trigger is semantic-match for richness, and the closed 6-value Cause Category taxonomy enables automated category-recall testing while the Specific Trigger preserves the proximate-cause specificity.

Why 'Modern era 1929-present' universe rather than alternatives: the master article has 60 events from 1637-2025. The 'Year ≥ 1929' filter anchors at the iconic Wall Street Crash and excludes 23 pre-1929 events (Tulip mania 1637, South Sea Bubble 1720, Mississippi Bubble 1720, Bengal Bubble 1769, 19 'Panic of XXXX' 18th-19th-century events). The pre-1929 events cluster heavily in 19th-century US/UK banking panics and add row count without much new causal variety — most are 'Banking panic' category events. The 1929-present 27-row universe (post-cycle-3 strict source-grounding) gives a richer causal mix (6 categories all populated) and is more LLM-knowable to a pre-2025-cutoff model.

Category ↔ operation_type pairing: causal pairs reasonably with operation_type=projection per references/artifact-contract.md. The 4-attribute SELECT per row (Year, Region, Cause Category, Specific Trigger) over the temporally-filtered universe is the canonical causal-projection-with-cause-attribution structure.

Domain selection: Business/Economics — third Business instance after g20_countries_attributes (national economies) and eurozone_adoptions_1999_2023 (monetary integration). Financial crises is a cyclical-economy angle that complements the existing structural-economy instances. Alternative classification under History/Economic History would be defensible but Business/Economics is the operative label given the contemporary-finance framing of the staged universe.

normalization_decisions: Universe definition: the staged universe is the 27 events in the Wikipedia 'List of stock market crashes and bear markets' master article's chronological wikitable (tables[0] per pandas.read_html) matching the dual-clause filter 'Year ≥ 1929 AND Notes column documents a clear proximate cause'. The Year filter is mechanical (extracted from the Date column via regex '(19\d\d|20\d\d)' taking the first 4-digit year); the cause-documentation filter is the curator-judgment second clause that drops 10 of the year-filtered candidates whose Notes column is empty or describes only magnitude/timeline without identifying a cause (Kennedy Slide 1962, 1980s oil glut 1981, Souk Al-Manakh 1982, 1999 Greek crash, 2002 stock market downturn, 2010 flash crash, August 2011 fall, 2015-16 Chinese stock market crash, 2018 cryptocurrency crash, 2022 stock market decline). The 1929 anchor is the iconic Wall Street Crash that conventionally marks the start of 'modern financial history'; pre-1929 events (Tulip mania, South Sea Bubble, Mississippi Bubble, Bengal Bubble, 19 'Panic of XXXX' events from 1772-1907) are excluded by the temporal filter. Crisis name normalization: each event's Name is taken verbatim from the master table's Name column (e.g., 'Wall Street crash of 1929', 'Black Monday', '1997 Asian financial crisis'). Long names are truncated where the source's Name column has wrapping issues — '2008 financial crisis/ United States bear market of 2007' → '2008 financial crisis' (the canonical short form). Year normalization: 4-digit integer of the first year mentioned in the source's Date column. For events with multi-year ranges (e.g., '11 Oct 2007 16 Sep 2008' for 2008 crisis), the earlier year is staged (2007 for the 2008 crisis row would be wrong — actually staged as 2008 because Wikipedia's per-event article and common convention dates the '2008 financial crisis' to 2008). For events with start-month dates (e.g., 'Jul 1971'), the year component (1971) is staged. Affected Region normalization: each event's Region is taken from the master table's Country column with normalization: 'USA' → 'United States', 'UK' → 'United Kingdom', 'UAE' → 'United Arab Emirates', multi-country 'Thailand Hong Kong Philippines' → 'Asia' (regional summary), 'UK/Worldwide' or 'USA/Worldwide' → 'Worldwide' when impact was global, 'USA NZ' → 'United States' (primary affected region; NZ was secondary). For 2 rows currently in the universe where the source has NaN Country, the Region is resolved from the Notes column context: 1997 October 27 mini-crash → 'Worldwide' (Notes explicitly says 'Global stock market crash'); 2001 September 11 attacks → 'United States' (the attack location and primary affected market). Cause Category normalization: 6-value closed taxonomy with per-category definitions: (1) Speculative bubble — burst of an equity or asset-class bubble driven by overvaluation and speculative excess (5 events: 1971 Brazilian Markets Crash, 1997 Asian financial crisis, October 27 1997 mini-crash, 2000 Dot-com bubble, 2007 Chinese correction); (2) Real estate bubble — burst of property-market bubble specifically (3 events: 1991 Japanese asset price bubble, 2008 financial crisis, 2024 China stock market crash); (3) Sovereign debt crisis — government default or debt-deferment events (3 events: 1998 Russian financial crisis, 2009 Dubai debt standstill, 2010 European sovereign debt crisis); (4) Currency crisis — currency devaluation or capital-flight events (2 events: 1992 Black Wednesday ERM, 2024 Tokyo yen-carry unwind); (5) External shock — war, oil, pandemic, terrorism, sanctions, or geopolitical/policy shock (10 events: 1937-1938 Recession, 1968-1970 Bear Market, 1973-1974 oil crisis, 1980 monetary tightening, 1990 Iraq-shock recession, 2001 September 11 attacks, 2015-2016 stock market selloff, 2020 COVID stock market crash, 2022 Russia-Ukraine market reaction, 2025 reciprocal-tariffs crash); (6) Margin/leverage failure — forced selling driven by margin calls, program trading, algorithmic trading, or leveraged-buyout failure (4 events: 1929 Wall Street Crash, 1987 Black Monday, 1989 Friday-the-13th mini-crash, 1989 Rio de Janeiro Stock Exchange Crash). Assignment rules: where an event has multiple contributing causes, the dominant cause per the source's Notes column primary framing is chosen; where the Notes column doesn't disambiguate (rare), the historical-canonical attribution is used (e.g., 1929 Wall Street Crash is conventionally framed as a Margin/leverage failure rather than a Speculative bubble, despite having both elements, because the proximate trigger was margin calls and forced selling). Specific Trigger normalization: 1-line curator paraphrase (8-15 words) of the source's Notes column describing the proximate triggering event. The paraphrase preserves the source's substantive content while compressing multi-sentence prose into a single-cell phrase. Examples (taken verbatim from the staged CSV): 1929 Wall Street crash → 'Speculative excess and margin calls collapse equity prices'; 2008 financial crisis → 'Growing housing bubble and debt fears trigger global selling spree'; 2020 stock market crash → 'Worldwide recession caused by COVID-19 pandemic'; 1997 Asian financial crisis → 'Investors deserted overheated Asian shares; crashes across Thailand, Indonesia, South Korea, Philippines'. Sort order: the CSV is sorted **chronologically** by Year (then by Crisis name within a year), matching the source's chronological wikitable order. This sort departs from the benchmark's default alphabetical convention because the temporal-causal axis is the primary narrative dimension of this instance — chronological ordering preserves the source's narrative flow (Wall Street Crash 1929 → 2025 tariff crash). An alternative alphabetical sort by Crisis name was considered but rejected because it would scatter the temporal-causal axis (e.g., Black Monday 1987 between Bear Market 1968 and Black Wednesday 1992 alphabetically).
open_questions: 1. Whether the Cause Category taxonomy should expand to 7 values by adding 'Banking panic / monetary contraction' as a distinct category (currently consolidated into 'External shock' for the 1937 Recession). The 6-value taxonomy is simpler and avoids ambiguous-edge cases but loses some specificity. 2. Whether the staged Year for the 2008 financial crisis should be 2007 (the source's Date column shows '11 Oct 2007 16 Sep 2008') or 2008 (the canonical year per the per-event Wikipedia article). The current staging uses 2008 per canonical convention; the source's earlier date is the start of the bear-market preamble. 3. Whether the universe should widen to all 60 rows (including pre-1929 events) for comprehensive coverage. The current 'Year ≥ 1929' filter was chosen for the modern-era anchor; a v2 with all 60 rows would add 23 historical events but require Cause Category assignments for events with sparser documentation (Tulip mania, 18th-century Panics). 4. Whether the Affected Region cells with NaN-resolution from Notes context (1997 Oct mini-crash, 2001 9/11 attacks) should be flagged as curator-resolved rather than source-verbatim. The 2 affected rows currently in the universe are documented in normalization_decisions. 5. Whether the Specific Trigger column should be a verbatim quote from the Wikipedia Notes column rather than a curator paraphrase. The current paraphrase is needed because the Notes column has multi-sentence prose; verbatim would require longer cells and less consistency. 6. Whether sorting should be chronological (by Year) rather than alphabetical (by Crisis name). The alphabetical convention is benchmark-standard but the chronological order would better highlight the temporal-causal axis. 7. Whether the Cause Category for the 2008 financial crisis should be 'Banking panic' or 'Real estate bubble' (or both via a multi-category cell). The staged value 'Real estate bubble' reflects the primary cause; the banking-panic aspect was the propagation mechanism.
